description: Somos Los Ratatopos Marcianos y participamos en NASA Space Apps 2026 con el desafío «Abandonados pero no olvidados». Queremos contar, mediante una historia ilustrada, la misión de Sojourner, el rover que exploró Marte en 1997. Buscamos compañeros con interés en investigar, redactar, dibujar, crear ilustraciones, consultar fuentes científicas y comunicar ideas. No necesitas experiencia previa: valoramos la creatividad, el compromiso y las ganas de aprender y trabajar en equipo.
summary:
**Archive of the Forgotten** is an interactive educational website developed by **Los Ratatopos Marcianos** to preserve and share the stories of spacecraft, scientific instruments, and exploration equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

Our project transforms publicly available NASA mission information into an accessible digital museum. Visitors can explore interactive planetary visualizations, select blue markers representing approximate mission locations, and discover 24 historical records containing mission descriptions, photographs, and educational context.

The experience also includes illustrated comics featuring our original team mascot, interactive timelines, a comparison of the Moon and Mars, and a final knowledge challenge.

By combining historical space exploration resources with web technology and creative storytelling, our project encourages curiosity, scientific learning, and appreciation for the legacy of space exploration.
details:
How does the project work?

Archive of the Forgotten is a browser-based interactive museum focused on the history of exploration equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

Users begin on a space-themed landing page and choose between two destinations. Each world features an interactive planetary visualization with blue markers representing approximate locations associated with historical missions. Selecting a marker allows users to explore the corresponding object or mission.

The museum includes 24 historical records: 12 related to the Moon and 12 related to Mars. These records combine descriptions, historical context, and mission imagery.

Educational features

The platform offers several complementary learning experiences:

  • Interactive exploration: users rotate planetary visualizations and investigate mission markers.
  • Historical records: visitors learn about spacecraft, scientific instruments, landers, and rovers.
  • Original educational comics: the Ratatopo mascot helps communicate historical events through illustrated storytelling.
  • Timeline: visitors follow major milestones in lunar and Martian exploration.
  • World Comparison: users compare environmental conditions on the Moon and Mars and their effects on historical artifacts.
  • Final Challenge: an interactive quiz reinforces learning.

Technology and NASA resources

The project uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to deliver an interactive web experience accessible through a browser.

Publicly available NASA mission archives, scientific information, and historical photographs support the educational content. Approximate marker locations are educational interpretations developed by our team using historical mission references; they are not presented as NASA-certified coordinates.

Creativity and impact

Our main innovation is combining scientific history, interactive planetary exploration, original comics, and game-based learning in one accessible digital museum.

The project aims to inspire students and the general public to discover the history of space exploration and understand why equipment left on other worlds remains scientifically and historically significant.
